sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis d ≥ 2 (or X(R) = ∅); the proof, which goes through Proposition 3.9, needs d ≥ 2 when X(R) ≠ ∅.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample in dimension one: X = E, the real elliptic curve y² = x³ − x. Here H²(E, O_E) = 0 and the Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles (codimension 0) holds. The only geometrically irreducible curve in E is E itself, of geometric genus 1, so the left side fails. Since E(R) ≠ ∅, Br(R) → Br(E) is injective and Pic(E) → Pic(E_C)^G is an isomorphism, so the right side holds. Proposition 3.9 (a curve of odd geometric genus exists) is stated for dimension ≥ 2, as the introduction says (p.4). The surface and higher-dimensional cases, which are the paper's applications, are unaffected. Found by the extraction (items printed-even-genus, main-even-genus).
